newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Resources buying LL&E for $3 billion.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Resources buying LL&E for $3 billion.

text.p: Burlington Resources Inc. said Thursday it will acquire Louisiana Land and Exploration Co. in a $3 billion stock deal that will form one of the nation's biggest independent energy exploration and production companies.

Under terms of the agreement, a subsidiary of Burlington Resurces will acquire LL&E in an exchange of stock in which LL&E shareholders will receive 1.525 shares of Burlington for each LL&E share they hold.

Based on Burlington's closing price of $46.125 Wednesday, the company said, the transaction has a total value of about $3.03 billion, including Burlington's assumption of about $500 million of LL&E debt.

That would value LL&E's stock at about $69.20. After the announcement Thursday, LL&E's shares shot up $9.875 to $67.375 on the New York Stock Exchange, where they were amoung the most heavily traded issues.
Burlington's shares lost 87.5 cents to $45.25, reducing the value of the deal to about $2.98 billion.

The combined company -- with operating cash flow of $1 billion a year and market capitalisation of $8.2 billion -- will be known as Burlington Resources. Its headquarters will be in Houston, where Burlington is already based.
Upon completion of the deal, Burlington President and Chief Executive Bobby Shackouls will become chairman, president and CEO of the combined company.
H. Leighton Steward, chairman, president and CEO of New Orleans-based LL&E, will become vice chairman and chairman of the executive committee of the board.
As of the end of last year the two companies on a combined basis had domestic gas reserves of 5.9 trillion cubic feet and production of 1.5 billion cubic feet per day.
Current combined worldwide natural gas production is 1.7 billion cubic feet per day and liquids production is about 90,000 barrels per day, the announcement said.
The companies said they expected the deal to be accounted for as a pooling of interests and to qualify as a tax-free reorganization.
They added that the combination would add to cash flow starting this year.
